decisions.decision: Use PyIceberg SqlCatalog with SQLite backend
decisions.rationale: Zero infrastructure requirement. SQLite is file-based, works everywhere, survives process restarts. No catalog server needed.

decisions.decision: Use PyIceberg for writes, DuckDB for analytical reads
decisions.rationale: DuckDB Iceberg extension is read-only as of v1.5.0. PyIceberg is the standard write path for the ecosystem.

decisions.decision: Arrow bridge pattern for time travel reads (PyIceberg scan → Arrow → DuckDB)
decisions.rationale: DuckDB's native iceberg_scan with version parameter silently ignores the snapshot version and returns the latest state. Tested on DuckDB 1.5.0 + PyIceberg 0.11.1. PyIceberg scan correctly filters by snapshot_id, and the Arrow bridge to DuckDB works flawlessly.
decisions.discovery: iceberg_scan(path, version := snap_id) does NOT provide snapshot isolation. This is a critical finding — the project MUST use PyIceberg scan for all time travel queries.
alternatives_considered: DuckDB iceberg_scan with version parameter (tested, does not work for time travel)

decisions.decision: DuckDB iceberg_scan retained for current-state reads only
decisions.rationale: iceberg_scan works correctly for reading the latest state of an Iceberg table. Useful as an alternative read path when time travel is not needed.

known_limitations: DuckDB iceberg_scan does not support snapshot-based time travel (version parameter is unreliable)
PyIceberg SQLite catalog is single-user — no concurrent write support
DuckDB Iceberg extension is read-only — all writes must go through PyIceberg
